Title:DEBATE ON ANNUAL BUDGET STATEMENT
MPs Speaking:Dr Goh Keng Swee (Minister for Finance); Dr Lee Siew Choh (Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs); Dr Toh Chin Chye (Deputy Prime Minister and Leader of the House); Inche Yaacob Bin Mohamed (Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development); Mr Chan Sun Wing (Parliamentary Secretary to the Prime Minister); Mr Goh Chew Chua (Parliamentary Secretary to the Deputy Prime Minister); Mr K. Rajaratnam (Minister for Culture); Mr Wee Toon Boon (Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Labour and Law); Mr Yong Nyuk Lin (Minister for Education); Dato Abdul Hamid Bin Haji Jumat; Inche Ahmad Jabri Bin Mohammad Akib; Inche Baharuddin Bin Mohamed Ariff; Inche Mohd. Ali Bin Alwi; Mr A. P. Rajah; Mr C. H. Koh; Mr Ong Eng Guan; Mr S. Ramaswamy; Mr Thio Chan Bee; Mrs Seow Peck Leng; Tun Lim Yew Hock; Mr G. Kandasamy (Deputy Speaker); Sir George Oehlers (Mr Speaker);


Column: 80

ANNUAL BUDGET STATEMENT


am proud to say that my colleagues (not just in the Cabinet), my supporting team of Parliamentary Secretaries and Assemblymen have basic dedication, not selfishness. You will remember some Members in the last Assembly, Sir - Mr Lazarous, Mr Lee Choon Eng and Mr Mak Pak Shee. Sometimes I think we ought to cleanse our past, but whatever our other shortcomings, we have given an honest and effective government; and the business of a government is to govern in the interest of the people. We have come to grips with our problems after 1½ years. We are beginning to produce results. We will continue to press on, and I hope in the coming years, or even in the coming months, even the Member for Farrer Park would find it difficult to say that his is the best. As for the hon. the leader of the Opposition, if he were honest in not wishing to make political mention of the fact that he is in the Opposition, he would say that, knowing the trials and tribulations that the country was faced with, knowing what he had been in for in the last four years from 1955 to 1959, he never expected that there could emerge a government able to maintain the State, to give it coherence and purpose, and to make progress.

9.03 p m.

    Dr Goh Keng Swee rose -

    Mr Speaker: In reply?
